concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
question: Mahavdev Govind Ranade devoted his entire life to the _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Prarthana Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahadev Govind Ranade was one of the founding members of the **Prarthana Samaj**, established in 1867 in Bombay.
 
• The Prarthana Samaj focused on **social reforms**, including abolition of caste discrimination, widow remarriage, and women's education.
 
• Ranade was deeply influenced by the teachings of social reformers like **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** and focused on modernization within the framework of Indian traditions.
 
• He advocated for **inter-religious harmony** and promoted religious and social ideals that were progressive for his time.
 
• Mahadev Govind Ranade is often referred to as the **"Father of Indian Social Reform"** due to his significant contributions to social justice and equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prarthana Samaj**

 
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the **Brahmo Samaj** and aimed at creating a liberal and inclusive religious movement.
 
• It emphasized **monotheism** and rejected idol worship while advocating for ethical and moral living.
 
• The Samaj was instrumental in promoting social causes, including better treatment of women and eradication of societal evils.
 
 
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade**
 
 
• Ranade was an Indian scholar, social reformer, and jurist who worked for the upliftment of marginalized communities.
 
• He co-founded institutions like the **Widow Marriage Association** and the **Pune Sarvajanik Sabha**.
 
• He believed in gradual reform and modernization without disrupting the cultural fabric of India.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Movements in India**
 
 
• Movements like the Prarthana Samaj, Brahmo Samaj, and Arya Samaj were crucial in addressing issues like caste discrimination and women's rights.
 
• These movements were pivotal in laying the foundation for India's freedom struggle and progress toward equality.
